chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the traveler praying behind the resident. He said, 'He prays two rak'ahs and proceeds wherever he wishes.'

key_terms.اَلْمُسَافِرِ: The traveler (one on a journey with shortened prayer)

ai.seo_question: How should a traveler pray behind a resident according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the procedural aspect of *qasr* (shortened prayer) for a traveler leading or following a resident, emphasizing the brevity of the traveler's obligation. It highlights the practical flexibility granted to the *musafir*, allowing him to conclude his two-rak'ah prayer and resume his journey immediately, reflecting the ease (*rukhsah*) inherent in travel jurisprudence. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh for understanding the distinction between the full four-rak'ah prayer of the *muqim* and the two-rak'ah prayer of the *musafir* in congregational settings.
